title: Naples / Tunis
hook: 1200 → 1500. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Naples / Tunis in 1200 and 1500, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 1200 and 1500; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Naples area anchor: 14.195216, 40.906569 (8.9 km from the nominal location); Tunis area anchor: 10.18, 36.81 (0 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 1200 and 1500 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["Duchy of Benevento"],["Fatimid Caliphate"]],[["Aragón"],["Hafsid Caliphate"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1200.geojson (SHA-256 2d6913ecedb38e269e41d249c87874d81e3e8d7351754821f57e627442d91525); GeoJSON features [[45],[46]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1500.geojson (SHA-256 d01ffc9b80629787f13d2b1c2f881f005bc0164433548e30f5c058ddee0bfc7b); GeoJSON features [[270],[41]]

claims.text: At the two points, 1200 has different labels and 1500 has different labels. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1200.geojson (SHA-256 2d6913ecedb38e269e41d249c87874d81e3e8d7351754821f57e627442d91525); GeoJSON features [[45],[46]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1500.geojson (SHA-256 d01ffc9b80629787f13d2b1c2f881f005bc0164433548e30f5c058ddee0bfc7b); GeoJSON features [[270],[41]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: A historical border is drawn as a crisp line. What should you check before treating it as exact? Answer: The source's precision and limitations Rendering a precise-looking line cannot make an approximate reconstruction exact.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[5]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

recall.question: A historical border is drawn as a crisp line. What should you check before treating it as exact?
options: Whether the fill colour is dark
recall.why: Rendering a precise-looking line cannot make an approximate reconstruction exact.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
